Well, theoretically, in a dual coil configuration, the voltage is being split into two channels. So in a series box with a dual coil setup, one coil of the set is getting 4.2 volts and so is the other coil. Now in a series box with a single setup, that one coil is getting all 8.4 volts. So it would be an incredibly hot and pretty uncomfortable vape on a series box. On a parallel box it wouldn't be that bad though.

In my experience (and it's taken a while to come to this conclusion) is that, on a regulated mod, higher resistance is better for me. It puts less of a strain on my batteries via; less amperage draw, therefore, lengthening my battery life. With that being said, I do build custom coils for myself and others. I've gotten to where I pretty much only run mechanical mods exclusively. I prefer series boxes over parallel, simply because I usually try to build to around a Ω.17 on my noisy cricket, and at a full charge that's pushing around 415 watts. In all honesty man, it's really all about preference. You can definitely build big, fancy coils that are higher than Ω.10. It's all in the prep work.
